zakat.subtitle: Corporate Zakat calculation per Sharia principles
zakat.islamic_note: Zakat applies to Muslim-majority countries (Saudi Arabia, UAE, etc.)
zakat.zatca_note_desc: The official method approved by ZATCA (Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority). Base = Equity + Long-term Liabilities + Provisions + Profit - Fixed Assets - Long-term Investments.
zakat.aaoifi_note_desc: Per AAOIFI standards and scholarly consensus: Base = Cash + Trade Goods + Collectible Receivables + Trading Investments - Current Liabilities (Short-term Debts). Excludes: Fixed assets, intangibles, and WIP.
zakat.sharia_method_desc: Uses only the Assets side of the balance sheet — Zakat is due on Cash and Trade Goods only. Excludes liabilities, receivables, investments, and fixed assets. (No double-counting in Zakat)
zakat.zatca_warning: ZATCA method calculates from both sides of the balance sheet (liabilities and assets) which may lead to double-counting (Zakat duplication). The Sharia Assets method is recommended.
zakat.excluded_reason: These assets are excluded because they are neither cash nor trade goods — no Zakat is due on them (incomplete ownership or consumable assets)
